defects.note: root/t10/secret has the prefix root/t1, so tenant t1 reads and writes tenant t10's files with a name of ../t10/secret (percent-encoded past the mux). Compare against dir plus the separator, or open through os.Root

the allowance is read under the lock, the file is written, and used is charged under a second lock hold; two concurrent uploads by one tenant both see the same remaining and both fit, so the quota is exceeded by up to one upload per concurrent request

map iteration order is random per range, so a file with two labels hashes to a different tag on each call and the 304 the doc promises never happens; sort the keys first. The test uses one label and cannot see it
Delete removes the file and the index entry but never subtracts the size from used, so a tenant that stores and deletes is locked out of its quota for good

WriteTimeout covers the whole response, and the server exists to send files of up to 256 MiB: any download that takes longer than ten seconds is cut mid-body. Bound headers with ReadHeaderTimeout and leave the body to the client's context, or set it per handler with http.ResponseController
//evil.example/ starts with a slash and is a protocol-relative URL, so the browser leaves the site; parse next and require an empty Scheme and Host, or a path that starts with a single slash

the type is whatever the uploader sent, served inline from the vault's origin with no X-Content-Type-Options and no Content-Disposition: an uploaded text/html file runs as the vault. Serve as attachment with nosniff, or from a separate origin

the first X-Forwarded-For entry is whatever the client wrote; the proxy appends the peer it saw last. A client that rotates the header has an unlimited upload allowance. Take the last entry, or only trust the header from the proxy's address

the deferred Put runs before the caller writes the bytes, and Bytes aliases the buffer, so another request can Get the same buffer and overwrite the body mid-flight: one tenant's listing goes out to another. Return a copy, or write the response before Put
the test compares the message of a sentinel the package exports; errors.Is(err, ErrBadName) survives a reworded message and a wrap

the upload is copied straight into its final name, so a concurrent Open serves a half-written file, and the stat fallback reports its partial size as the truth. Write to a temporary name in the same directory and rename

defects.match: m := Meta{Name: name, Size: n, ContentType: contentType, ModTime: time.Now(), Labels: labels}
defects.note: the caller's labels map is stored by reference and handed back out by List and Open in every Meta; a caller that changes its map changes the index and the ETag. maps.Clone on the way in
a 304 carries the ETag the 200 would have carried (RFC 9110 §15.4.5); set the header before the If-None-Match check

baits.note: omitzero (Go 1.24) is the option that omits a zero time.Time; omitempty never omits a struct

baits.match: if err := s.audit(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), ev); err != nil {
baits.note: the audit entry must be written even when the client has gone; WithoutCancel keeps the request's values and drops its cancellation, which is what go-context prescribes

baits.match: _, _ = w.Write(body) // headers are sent; a failed write is the client's disconnect
baits.note: the discard is deliberate and carries its reason; the body is JSON under an explicit application/json type. gosec G705 reports the line as XSS through taint analysis, which is the tool being wrong
